slo_title: Apply their understanding of heat conduction models to solve similar examples.

mcq.q: \(\text{The one-dimensional heat equation that describes temperature distribution in a rod is:}\)
\(\text{For the heat equation with zero temperature at both ends, the proper transient solution is:}\)

options.C: \(u(x,t) = (A e^{\lambda x} + B e^{-\lambda x})e^{\alpha^2\lambda^2 t}\)

mcq.q: \(\text{The one-dimensional wave equation that describes the transverse vibrations of a string is:}\)
\(\text{For a string with initial displacement } y(x,0)=a\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{l}\right) \text{ and zero initial velocity, the solution is:}\)
\(\text{When solving the heat equation with zero boundary conditions and initial temperature } u(x,0)=f(x), \text{ the coefficients are found by:}\)

options.A: \(\text{Expanding } f(x) \text{ in a Fourier cosine series}\)
options.B: \(\text{Expanding } f(x) \text{ in a Fourier half-range sine series}\)

mcq.answer_text: \(\text{Expanding } f(x) \text{ in a Fourier half-range sine series}\)

sq.q: \(\text{A rod of length } \pi \text{ has ends at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=x(\pi-x). \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Boundary conditions: } u(0,t)=0, u(\pi,t)=0. \text{ Initial condition: } u(x,0)=x(\pi-x).\)
\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)

sq.q: \(\text{A rod of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{l}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Boundary conditions: } u(0,t)=0, u(l,t)=0. \text{ Initial condition: } u(x,0)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{l}.\)
\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

lq.q: \(\text{Solve the vibrating string problem: $\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}, 0 $with $y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0, y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right), y_t(x,0)=0.$}\\ \text{Also solve the heat equation: $ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}, 0$ with $u(0,t)=0, u(\pi,t)=0, u(x,0)= x.$}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{String problem: general solution \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{\(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0.\) \(y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right)+ \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_2=1, C_4=1,\) others zero.}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi c t}{l}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Heat equation: general solution \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{\(u(x,0)= x = \sum B_n \sin(nx).\) Compute \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} x \sin(nx) dx.\)}\) \(\text{Integration: \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left[ \dfrac{-x \cos(nx)}{n} + \dfrac{\sin(nx)}{n^2} \right]_0^{\pi} = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(\dfrac{-\pi \cos(n\pi)}{n}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{n} \cos(n\pi) = \dfrac{2}{n}(-1)^{n+1}.\)}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{2(-1)^{n+1}}{n} \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks) Combine both solutions. (1 Mark) Discuss physical difference: heat solution decays exponentially, wave solution oscillates indefinitely. (2 Marks)
